html:
Arakan is the coastal strip along the Bay of Bengal in what is now western Myanmar, today's Rakhine State. It was home to a series of kingdoms for over a thousand years, and the map shows it from the 1st century to 1815.

Mountains cut Arakan off from the Irrawaddy valley, so it looked west and by sea as much as east. Its early kingdoms, centred on Dhanyawadi and later Waithali, left inscriptions in Sanskrit and Buddhist and Hindu images that show close ties to India.

Its golden age came under the kingdom of Mrauk U, founded in 1429 by a king who had regained his throne with help from the Bengal Sultanate. For a time its kings paid tribute to Bengal and used Muslim titles alongside Buddhist ones.

  • In the 1500s and 1600s Mrauk U was a rich port city with a strong navy.
  • It hired Portuguese mercenaries and raided the Bengal delta for slaves.
  • It held Chittagong until the Mughals took it in 1666.

The kingdom weakened through the 1700s. In 1784 and 1785 King Bodawpaya of Konbaung Burma conquered it and carried off the Mahamuni Buddha, Arakan's holiest image, to his capital. Refugees fleeing into British Bengal helped spark the First Anglo-Burmese War, after which Britain took Arakan in 1826. The mix of Buddhist Rakhine and Muslim communities is the background to the Rohingya crisis of recent years.
sum: Arakan is the coastal strip along the Bay of Bengal in what is now western Myanmar, today's Rakhine State. It was home to a series of kingdoms for over a thousand years, and the map shows it from the 1st century to 1815.
